tasks.title: Implement and test email address validation
tasks.acceptance_criterion: The public isValidEmail(value) API returns true for person@example.com; returns false without throwing for person, @example.com, person@, whitespace-only strings, leading- or trailing-whitespace addresses, and non-string values; and the full test suite passes.
tasks.deterministic_validity_check: node -e "const assert=require('node:assert/strict'); const api=require('./src/index.js'); assert.equal(typeof api.isValidEmail,'function'); assert.equal(api.isValidEmail('person@example.com'),true); for (const value of ['person','@example.com','person@','   ',' person@example.com','person@example.com ',null,undefined,42,{},[]]) assert.doesNotThrow(()=>assert.equal(api.isValidEmail(value),false));"
patch_requirements: Create a reusable email validator that performs only local practical syntax validation and returns a boolean for every input.
Export the validator from src/index.js as isValidEmail.
Reject leading or trailing whitespace instead of trimming it.
Add regression tests covering the accepted common address and every malformed or non-string category named by the acceptance criterion.
Do not add network calls, DNS lookups, mailbox checks, or new dependencies.
